items.followUp: Define transpiration and describe the path water vapour takes from mesophyll cells to the atmosphere.

accept: loss of water in the form of water vapour
rubric.why: The definition must identify water vapour as the form of water lost and the aerial parts as its source.
rubric.how: Award for defining transpiration as the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.

rubric.why: This is the first event in stomatal transpiration: water evaporates from mesophyll cell surfaces into the leaf air spaces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that water evaporates from moist mesophyll cell walls into the intercellular spaces.

rubric.why: This identifies how water vapour passes from the leaf air spaces out of the leaf.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that water vapour diffuses through the air spaces and exits through the stomatal pore into the atmosphere.

rubric.why: These labels identify the main relevant parts in a section of the leaf.
rubric.how: Award for a section diagram that labels the mesophyll, guard cells and stomatal pore (or stoma).

rubric.why: The arrows should show the direction of water vapour movement from the mesophyll, through the leaf air spaces and out of a stoma.
rubric.description: Direction of vapour movement in the diagram
rubric.how: Award for arrows showing vapour moving from the mesophyll into the air spaces and out through the stomatal pore.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant.
Water evaporates from the moist walls of mesophyll cells into the intercellular spaces of the leaf.
Water vapour diffuses through the air spaces and out through the stomatal pore into the atmosphere.
Section diagram: draw and label the upper epidermis, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll, intercellular air spaces, lower epidermis, guard cells and stomatal pore.
Draw arrows from mesophyll cell surfaces into the air spaces and then out through the stomatal pore.

items.followUp: Compare active and passive transport, stating the energy requirement and direction of movement for each.

rubric.why: Active transport requires energy and moves substances against the concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for stating that active transport uses energy and moves substances from lower to higher concentration, against the concentration gradient.

rubric.why: Passive transport does not require cellular energy and moves substances down the concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for stating that passive transport does not use energy and moves substances from higher to lower concentration, down the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Active transport uses energy to move substances against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration.
Passive transport does not use energy; substances move down their concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration.
